subject: Road Traffic Victim Remembrance and Safety Advocacy
overview: Representatives from local advocacy groups discussed the city's official proclamation for road traffic victims and presented a multi-point platform for pedestrian and cyclist infrastructure improvements.

items.title: Preliminary comments on the Kyle Rittenhouse verdict
items.summary: Danielle Balocca offered opening remarks on the trial's outcome and its implications for community safety and systemic justice.

items.title: Proclamation of World Day of Remembrance for Road Traffic Victims
items.summary: The Mayor officially proclaimed the third Sunday of November as the World Day of Remembrance for Road Traffic Victims in Medford.

items.title: Walk Medford advocacy platform
items.summary: Ellery Klein presented a nine-point platform focusing on Complete Streets policies, safe school routes, and improving safety on state-owned DCR parkways.

items.title: Medford Bicycle Advisory Commission update
items.summary: Emily O'Brien discussed plans to update the city's bike master plan, increase bicycle rack availability, and improve wayfinding signage for regional paths.

items.title: Safe Roads Alliance legislative update
items.summary: Emily Stein outlined support for state legislation regarding automated speed enforcement cameras and the Vulnerable Road User bill for truck safety.

items.title: Public engagement and neighborhood traffic calming
items.summary: Speakers encouraged residents to join monthly advisory meetings and described 'neighbor ways' as a method for localized, resident-led traffic calming.
